inline.s: Where Master Hōnen Went Astray:
1. Distorting the Eighteenth Vow.
The
“even ten recitations” spoken of in the Eighteenth Vow
refers to ten continuous recitations at the time of death
. For the basis of this, see
The Eighteenth Vow

. Yet Master Hōnen distorted the “even ten recitations” of the Eighteenth Vow into the claim that merely reciting the Buddha’s name ten times with a scattered mind in daily life suffices for rebirth, and on this basis loudly preached that reciting the name guarantees birth.
He turned his back on the Dharma gate praised and embraced by Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Utmost Bliss—
the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception

The Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception is the “Dharma gate received and embraced by all Buddhas (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Utmost Bliss)” praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Utmost Bliss). In this sūtra, Śākyamuni Buddha says:

“Śāriputra, in the west as well there dwell at present the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Life, the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Skandhas, the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Light, the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Banner, the Tathāgata of Great Sovereignty, the Tathāgata of Great Light, the Tathāgata of Flaming Radiance, the Tathāgata of the Great Jewel Banner, and the Tathāgata of Radiant Light—Buddhas such as these, as many as the sands of the Ganges, dwelling each in his own pure Buddha land in the west. Each one manifests the sign of the broad and long tongue, covering the entire trichiliocosm, surrounding it on every side, and speaks these sincere and truthful words: You sentient beings should all believe and accept this ‘praise of the inconceivable merits of the Buddha land—the
Dharma gate
received and embraced by all Buddhas.’
Precisely because this is the

“Dharma gate received and embraced by all Buddhas (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Utmost Bliss)” praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Utmost Bliss)
Śākyamuni Buddha in this sūtra stresses again and again that one must ‘
practice as taught
The essence of this Dharma gate is:
continuous recollection without distraction, and birth in that Buddha land.
The sūtra says:

“Śāriputra, if there are good men or good women of pure faith who hear this name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life with its boundless and inconceivable merits, and the meritorious adornments of the Land of Utmost Bliss, and having heard them, reflect upon them—whether for one day and night, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven—
their recollection remains continuous and undistracted

. When such good men or good women approach the end of life, the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, together with his countless voice-hearer disciples and the host of bodhisattvas, surrounds them before and behind, comes to stand before them, and with compassion blesses and protects them so that their minds remain undisturbed. Once they have laid down their lives, they follow that Buddha’s assembly and are born in the pure Buddha land, the Land of Utmost Bliss of Immeasurable Life. And again, Śāriputra, seeing this great matter and cause of benefit and ease, I speak sincere and truthful words: if there are good men or good women of pure faith who hear this inconceivable meritorious name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life and this pure Buddha land of Utmost Bliss, they should all believe and accept, make the vow, and practice as taught,
being born in that Buddha land
That being so,
all
practitioners of the Pure Land school should
believe and accept, make the vow, practice as taught, and be born in that Buddha land
. (In the sūtra, the Buddha says:
all
should believe and accept, make the vow,
practice as taught,
and be born in that Buddha land.”
) So how did Master Hōnen conduct himself? In the Collected Writings of Master Hōnen
‘Questions and Answers,’ there is a record of “the question-and-answer with the Monk Myōhen,” transcribed below:
(the Monk Myōhen)
asked: ‘How can defiled ordinary beings such as we, in this evil world of the last age, escape birth and death?’
(Master Hōnen)
answered: ‘Simply by reciting Namo Amitabha Buddha and vowing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss, one can escape birth and death.’
He asked: ‘I know the Pure Land teaching says as much. Yet even while reciting the Buddha’s name, the mind is scattered—what then?’
He answered: ‘Even I, Hōnen
(as Master Hōnen refers to himself)
, am unable to achieve this.’
He asked: ‘Then what is to be done?’

He answered: ‘You should know that even with a scattered mind, one who recites the name, riding upon the power of the Buddha’s vow, is certain to attain rebirth. In a word, Buddha-recitation is the foremost matter.’
Myōhen said: ‘Yes, yes—it was to hear these words that I came.’

After the Monk had withdrawn, the Master said to the monks present: ‘Those born in the scattered lands of the desire realm all have scattered minds, just as one born in the human realm has eyes and a nose. To speak of “setting aside the scattered mind and attaining rebirth”—there is no such principle. Rebirth through scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely
(Amitabha Buddha’s)
supreme Primal Vow. This Monk’s question of “even while reciting the Buddha’s name, the mind is scattered—what then” is a superfluous matter.’
Translation:
The Monk Myōhen asked: “How can defiled ordinary beings such as we, in this evil world of the last age, escape birth and death?”
Master Hōnen answered: “Simply by reciting Namo Amitabha Buddha and vowing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss, one can escape birth and death.”
He asked: “I know the Pure Land teaching says as much. Yet even while reciting the Buddha’s name, the mind is scattered—what is to be done?”
He answered: “To recite the Buddha’s name without a scattered mind—even I myself cannot do that.”
He asked: “Then what should be done?”

He answered: “You should know that even with a scattered mind, one who recites the name, riding upon the power of the Buddha’s vow, is certain to attain rebirth. In a word, Buddha-recitation is the foremost matter.”
The Monk Myōhen said: “Yes, yes—it was to hear these words that I came.”

After the Monk Myōhen had withdrawn, Master Hōnen said to the monks present: “Those born in the scattered lands of the desire realm all have scattered minds, just as one born in the human realm has eyes and a nose. To speak of ‘setting aside the scattered mind and attaining rebirth’—there is no such principle! Rebirth through scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely Amitabha Buddha’s supreme Primal Vow. This question of the Monk Myōhen—‘even while reciting the Buddha’s name, the mind is scattered—what then’—is entirely superfluous.”
Commentary:

This question of the Monk Myōhen—‘even while reciting the Buddha’s name, the mind is scattered—what then’—is by no means superfluous; it strikes at the very crux, for it is the key to whether one attains rebirth or not! The pity is that he asked the way of a blind man
, was deceived by Hōnen, and the two of them, hand in hand, fell into a pit of fire
. Who knows in which kalpa or which lifetime he will ever be able to raise his head again!

When the Monk Myōhen came to consult Master Hōnen, asking, “Even while reciting the Buddha’s name, the mind is scattered—what then?” he was in fact asking: how does one attain continuous recollection without distraction (single-mindedness without distraction)? For this is the key that ensures rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. Although Master Hōnen himself had not attained continuous recollection without distraction (“even I, Hōnen, am unable to achieve this”), they could perfectly well have explored and discussed together how such continuous, undistracted recollection is to be attained, while Hōnen himself earnestly practiced it, taking his whole life as the term, following the Buddha’s teaching:
“Though one toils for a single lifetime, in a mere instant thereafter one is born in the land of Immeasurable Life, with bliss beyond measure.”
(the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha)
But Hōnen both feared rigorous practice and craved fame, offerings, and gain. Therefore he not only failed to practice as taught in the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception,

but on the contrary said: “You should know that even with a scattered mind, one who recites the name, riding upon the power of the Buddha’s vow, is certain to attain rebirth.” This utterly contravenes the teaching of the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception; he preached “scattered-mind Buddha-recitation guarantees rebirth,” and even went so far as to say: “Rebirth through scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely (Amitabha Buddha’s) supreme Primal Vow.”
Obstinately following his own course, he strayed ever further
, and by distorting the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception (see
“Master Hōnen’s Distortion of the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception”
) and fabricating the Vast Vow Gate (see
“Master Hōnen’s Fabrication of the Vast Vow Gate”
) he built up a doctrinal system at once lazy and greedy, whose poison has spread for eight hundred years down to the present day.
Master Hōnen’s doctrinal system can be captured in a pair of couplets.
The first line reads:
Fabricating recklessly, the Dharma turned upside down;
The second line reads:
Lazy and greedy, goading others into evil.
Fabricating recklessly
For example,

Master Hōnen himself admitted that he had not even attained the most basic single-mindedness without distraction, yet his biography claims that he “attained samādhi in this very life”—would you believe it? These people will fabricate anything! And come to think of it, since Master Hōnen dared to fabricate even the Vast Vow Gate (
see
Master Hōnen’s Fabrication of the Vast Vow Gate

), what would his disciples and their disciples not dare to fabricate? Since Master Hōnen dared to distort even the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception, praised and embraced by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha), (see
“Master Hōnen’s Distortion of the Sūtra of Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception”

), what sūtra or treatise would his disciples and their disciples not dare to distort? In truth, Hōnen himself built his career on reckless fabrication; master and disciples follow one another in an unbroken line, handing it down from generation to generation,
fabricating recklessly
the Dharma turned upside down,
becoming the basic hallmark of their teaching

, and moreover, the more they fabricate the more outlandish it becomes (one need only look at Master Huijing’s The Essential Principles of the Pure Land School, Master Jingzong’s Master Shandao’s Pure Land Thought, and the Interview with Master Jingzong on the Buddhist Door Website), each generation outdoing the last.
[The Dharma turned upside down]
Master Hōnen

and his followers loudly preach: to be born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss one “need not cut off evil and cultivate good,” “need not observe the precepts,” “may commit evil and break the law as one pleases,” “the wicked are the true objects of Amitabha Buddha’s deliverance,” “reciting the name guarantees birth,” “the Vast Vow Gate,” and so forth;
see
The Primal Vow Dharma Gate Is a Heretical Path Disguised as Buddhism

[Lazy and greedy] By “lazy” is meant unwilling to practice with diligence, even fearing diligent practice, vainly hoping to gain without effort; by “greedy” is meant greedy for fame, for gain, for sensual pleasure, for the fruition of attainment.
Being both lazy and greedy, and inciting people to evil—this is the dominant theme of Master Hōnen’s doctrinal system.

[Inciting evil] The Primal Vow Dharma Gate holds that committing evil and breaking the law do not matter at all, and that monks may take wives and eat meat. Its scriptural text, The Doctrine of the Shin School, says: “Great as the offenses of ordinary beings may be, compared with the power of the Vow they are no more than a drop in the ocean (that is, great as the offenses of ordinary beings may be, compared with the power of Amitabha Buddha’s Vow they are like a single grain set against the great ocean—utterly insignificant. For the refutation of this fallacy, see
The Primal Vow Dharma Gate Is a Heretical Path Disguised as Buddhism

, Appendix Nine: Refuting “reciting the name guarantees birth” and “the wicked are the true objects of deliverance”), therefore it does not matter whether one eats meat or keeps a wife.” They loudly preach: there is no need to practice, no need to observe the precepts, no need to do good, no need to purify one’s own mind; even committing evil one’s whole life long does not matter, because the wicked are the true objects of Amitabha Buddha’s deliverance. For example, Master Huijing says: “They fail to see that the purpose of the Contemplation Sūtra is to reveal the Buddha’s Primal Vow: the wicked are the true objects of deliverance. ...... The Primal Vow Dharma Gate takes the wicked as the true objects of deliverance.” Master Xinyuan, a disciple who took refuge with Master Huijing, says: “Let us now look at Amitabha Buddha’s deliverance: which kind of being does it take as the true object? The wicked are the true objects of deliverance.” See
The Primal Vow Dharma Gate Is a Heretical Path Disguised as Buddhism
This
recklessly fabricating, Dharma-upside-down,
lazy, greedy, evil-inciting doctrinal system
, though it can cleverly exploit the weaknesses of human nature to gain a following, speaking as if flowers were raining from heaven, yet what is false is false after all
and practice proves everything
(see
The Practice of Master Hōnen’s Teaching

To teach while contravening the meaning of the sūtras, distorting the scriptures, and slandering the Buddha and the Dharma is impure preaching. For one who preaches the Dharma impurely, the offenses are extremely grave (greater than taking the lives of all beings in the trichiliocosm), the retribution is extremely fearsome (falling into the great hells), and the fate of his followers is likewise extremely tragic (once they have entered upon the wrong path it is hard to turn back; for a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand lifetimes they undergo ruin and distress, with suffering unceasing).
The Buddha said:
“Śāriputra, though a hateful enemy may take one’s life
(for vicious as a hateful enemy is, he takes only one’s life)
, one loses only a single body
(and the life taken is only of this one lifetime)
, but when such a deluded person preaches the Dharma impurely, he brings great ruin and distress upon living beings for tens of millions of billions of kalpas
(for his followers, with wrong views lodged in their minds, life after life through tens of millions of billions of kalpas, can hardly free themselves, and calamities follow one upon another)
. Such a person
(the person beguiled by impure preaching)

with ignorance and darkness, covers over the Buddha’s bodhi—the original mind; his craving flares up again, ceaselessly continuing, and because of that craving he wanders through the five paths, with no path of goodness, his birth and death unending. Therefore, Śāriputra,
one who preaches the Dharma impurely incurs a great deal of offense, serves living beings as a bad spiritual friend, and slanders the Buddhas of past, future, and present
. Śāriputra, setting aside all the living beings of this Jambudvīpa,
if someone were to take the lives of all the living beings of the trichiliocosm, the offense of preaching the Dharma impurely is greater still
. Why? Because such a person destroys the anuttarā samyak-saṃbodhi of the Buddhas and assists the work of demons,
and causes living beings to suffer ruin and distress for a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand lifetimes

; he can only bind, never release. You should know that such a person is a bad spiritual friend to living beings, and through this false speech slanders and reviles the Buddhas before the great assembly,
by this cause and condition he falls into the great hells
Therefore you should know:
such a person would rather cut out his own tongue with a sharp knife than preach the Dharma impurely in the assembly
(the Buddha Treasury Sūtra)

[The five paths] Heaven, human, hell, hungry ghosts, and animals. If one speaks of the six paths, the asuras are added. Here they are not mentioned because the path of the asuras is subsumed within the destinies of heaven, human, animal, and hungry ghost.
